debt.description: The central moral engine of Orzhov society. Debt is not merely financial — it is spiritual, political, and generational. The Syndicate ensures no debt is ever truly settled.
sub_themes: debt as identity and social station
debt.narrative_tension: Characters believe they can earn freedom by repaying; the system is designed so they never can.
sample_hooks: A stonemason's grandson discovers his family owes three generations of back-tithe to the Syndicate.
A ghost refuses to pass on, bound by a clause in her death contract she cannot read.
A clerk uncovers a ledger proving the high prelate himself is deeply in debt — to no one living.

hierarchy.description: Power in the Orzhov is inherited, purchased, or extorted — never earned through merit. The hierarchy is vertical, rigid, and self-reinforcing.
sub_themes: the Obzedat ghost council as pinnacle authority
tiered clergy ranks and their privileges
rank as performance — robes, seals, liturgical rights
hierarchy.narrative_tension: The hierarchy promises reward for loyalty but guarantees stasis.
sample_hooks: A young prelate realizes promotion is blocked by a ghost elder who died before giving way.
An enforcer is ordered to collect tithe from her own family.
A scribe discovers that the rank above hers has been vacant for forty years — intentionally.

law.description: Orzhov law is not justice. It is a codified mechanism for control, authored by those with the most to gain from its provisions.
sub_themes: contracts written in language designed to entrap
the legal personhood of the dead
the distinction between lawful and right
law.narrative_tension: The law is always technically obeyed; justice is never served.
sample_hooks: A defendant wins her case but learns the legal fees have exceeded her estate.
A ghost successfully sues a living heir for breach of posthumous contract.
An investigator proves fraud — and is immediately arrested for accessing sealed records.

extortion.description: The Syndicate monetizes every human vulnerability: grief, hope, fear of death, love of family. Extortion is not aberrant — it is the product offered.
sub_themes: resurrection as a service with recurring fees
extortion.narrative_tension: The victim must remain grateful to their extortioner.
sample_hooks: A merchant pays for guaranteed safe passage — then learns the threats were always from the Syndicate itself.
A widow's husband is resurrected and now owes a ten-year labor contract.
A child is offered a scholarship to the Syndicate's academy; the fine print assigns her future earnings.

sanctity.description: The Orzhov wraps all of the above in the language of the sacred. Ritual, vestment, and ceremony lend moral weight to systems of exploitation.
sub_themes: the performance of holiness as branding
the dead as saints — and assets
sanctity.narrative_tension: Genuine faith exists inside the structure and is weaponized against the faithful.
sample_hooks: A novice monk discovers the sacred relic he prays before is an IOU signed by the original donor.
A parishioner is excommunicated for missing a single tithe payment during illness.
A reformist priest attempts to hold mass for free — and is charged with unlicensed religious practice.

legacy.description: The Orzhov are obsessed with legacy: what is owed, what is owned, and what endures beyond death. Ghosts are not memories — they are stakeholders.
legacy.narrative_tension: The living serve the dead, and the dead serve the Syndicate.
sample_hooks: A family's patriarch has been dead for eighty years but still holds the deed to the house.
Two branches of a guild go to war over a will that may have been forged.
A ghost discovers that dying did not end her obligations — it added interest.

the_creditor.description: The one who holds the debt. May be living, dead, or institutional. Outwardly generous, structurally predatory.
the_creditor.motivation: Ensure the debt is never fully repaid; extract maximum value indefinitely.

the_debtor.description: The one who owes. Often inherited the debt rather than incurred it. Struggles between compliance and defiance.
the_debtor.motivation: Find a path to freedom within a system designed to prevent it.

the_enforcer.description: The instrument of the Syndicate's will. Believes in the law — or has stopped believing in anything.
the_enforcer.motivation: Execute orders and avoid becoming a cautionary tale.

the_ghost_elder.description: A Syndicate patriarch or matriarch who refused to let death interrupt business. Powerful, ancient, increasingly detached from the living.
the_ghost_elder.motivation: Preserve the Syndicate's power and their own relevance past death.

the_reformist.description: One who believes the system can be changed from within. Usually wrong. Sometimes right in ways they never intended.
the_reformist.motivation: Introduce genuine justice into a system that treats justice as overhead.

the_convert.description: Someone who joined the Syndicate willingly, seduced by its power, beauty, or promises — and now questions everything.
the_convert.motivation: Find a way out without becoming another asset.

inciting_incidents: A debt notice arrives with a name the protagonist does not recognize.
A family member dies and their ghost immediately begins demanding payment.
The Syndicate offers to solve a problem — and the protagonist accepts.
An enforcer is dispatched to collect from someone they love.
A reformist publishes a sermon that accidentally quotes a sealed Syndicate ledger.
midpoint_reversals: The protagonist discovers the debt they are trying to repay is structured to compound faster than payment.
An ally is revealed to be a Syndicate informant — but so conflicted they tip off the protagonist first.
The ghost the protagonist has been helping turns out to be the original creditor in disguise.
The legal loophole found to escape the contract creates a larger obligation.
The reformist's movement is co-opted and re-branded as a Syndicate charity.
climax_types: Expose the fraudulent ledger at the public reading of wills, forcing the Syndicate to acknowledge the debt is void.
Convince a ghost elder to release the debt in exchange for something only the protagonist can offer.
Burn the contract — knowing the Syndicate will retaliate but that the act itself is worth it.
Become a ghost voluntarily to gain standing in the Obzedat court and vote down the debt clause.
Discover the ghost council is itself bound by a contract no living person remembers signing.
resolution_types: Pyrrhic freedom: debt cancelled but protagonist loses everything else.
Compromise: partial relief, ongoing obligation, but survivable.
Tragic: protagonist becomes what they fought — a creditor.
Ambiguous: the contract is missing, the debt may be void, no one dares test it.
Triumphant: the system is exposed, the ghost council dissolves, but a new one forms within a generation.

protagonist_templates.label: The Heir
protagonist_templates.summary: Inherits debt they did not incur; must decide whether to honor it or contest it.

protagonist_templates.label: The Apostate
protagonist_templates.summary: Former Syndicate member who knows too much and fled — until the debt finds them.

protagonist_templates.label: The Investigator
protagonist_templates.summary: Hired to audit a Syndicate ledger; discovers systematic fraud that implicates everyone.

antagonist_templates.label: The Patient Patriarch
antagonist_templates.summary: A ghost elder who has been waiting centuries for this exact leverage.

antagonist_templates.label: The Smiling Prelate
antagonist_templates.summary: A living Syndicate leader who genuinely believes the system is just.

antagonist_templates.label: The Reluctant Enforcer
antagonist_templates.summary: Does not want to do this — but will.

supporting_templates.label: The Loyal Scribe
supporting_templates.summary: Knows where the bodies (and the ledgers) are buried.

supporting_templates.label: The Grieving Ghost
supporting_templates.summary: A recently deceased NPC still entangled in the system, able to provide insider access.

tone_registers.gothic_horror: Emphasize the physical weight of obligation: crumbling estates, ledgers written in blood, ghosts who cannot leave because the contract still binds them.
tone_registers.political_thriller: Focus on leverage, information asymmetry, and the slow exposure of institutional corruption.
tone_registers.dark_comedy: Play the bureaucratic absurdity straight — the ghost suing over a broken vase, the clerk who needs three forms to approve her own funeral.
tone_registers.tragedy: A character who genuinely believes in Orzhov values and discovers the institution they love is incapable of believing in them back.
tone_registers.heist: What would it take to steal, forge, or destroy the one document that could free an entire family? Who inside the Syndicate can be turned?

institutions: The Obzedat — the ghost council of dead patriarchs who still hold board seats
The Hall of Tithe — where all debts are registered and witnessed
The Pale Sanctum — the Syndicate's cathedral and financial headquarters
The Ossuary Vaults — archives of every contract ever written, guarded by spectral archivists
The Prelature — governing body of living clergy, technically subordinate to the Obzedat
artifacts_of_power: The Ledger of Last Resort — a tome that holds the master record of every outstanding debt
The Writ of Eternal Tithe — a self-replicating contract that adds new signatories automatically
The Coin of Absolution — redeemable for one act of forgiveness; there is only one, and it is never sold
The Ghost Bell — rung to summon a debtor's spirit back to testify against their heirs
geography: The Cloisters — residential towers for Syndicate clergy, hierarchically arranged by floor
Debtor's Row — the district where those who cannot pay are assigned labor contracts
The White Bridge — the formal border between civilian Ravnica and Orzhov territory, where tolls are collected
The Undercroft — sub-levels of the Pale Sanctum where enforcement operations are planned
